- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >+10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5-day prices as anchor for correction.
- If model forecast is >+5% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply “lag correction”: subtract 0.5–1% per day to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 70% of 30-day moving average, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1% to forecast to capture mean reversion.
